concept: Drawer is the side flap of an appliance slid open to show a list of the things the device keeps, such as its rooms, programs or filters. It stands at the inline end of the screen as a unit of its own, inset from every edge, and slides back in when you are done.

default_to_avoid.pattern: navigation drawer glued flush to the window edge, full height, with square corners (Material navigation drawer)
default_to_avoid.why_not: A panel fused to the window edge is a wall, not a unit, and P6 caps panels so they do not swell; the drawer keeps the panel radius and an inset gap on all four sides.

default_to_avoid.pattern: Drawer as a second Sheet that holds a device's controls
default_to_avoid.why_not: Sheet already holds one device's controls that act at once; the Drawer holds a list to pick from or filter by, so it fills the full height and scrolls its list between a fixed header and fixed keys.

references.source: Braun T 1000 world receiver (Dieter Rams, 1963): side flaps that open to show the band list and close flat against the case
Vitsoe 606 Universal Shelving (Dieter Rams, 1960): a vertical unit with a fixed header and a fixed inset on every side, never touching the wall by its own edge
WAI-ARIA Authoring Practices, Dialog (Modal) pattern: focus moves in, Tab stays inside, Escape closes, focus returns to the opener

derivation.consequence: sits where the hand expects it
derivation.form: The drawer slides in from the inline end, the right in left-to-right text, where the thumb of a held phone rests, and its one key sits at the bottom of the same column.

derivation.consequence: capped so large panels do not swell into pillows
derivation.form: The panel keeps corner.panel as its radius and an inset gap on all four sides, so a full-height panel stays a unit and never turns into a wall.

derivation.consequence: labels sit on the body's inset line, never floating mid-surface
derivation.form: The title and the close key share one header row on the top inset line, and the list and keys start on the same inline inset.

derivation.consequence: every mechanism has its keyboard map
derivation.form: Tab stays inside the drawer, Escape, the close key and a click on the scrim all close it, and focus goes back to the key that opened it.
The drawer slides in from its edge as one piece on the decelerating curve and leaves faster on the accelerating one; nothing inside it moves on its own.

options.name: full-height unit with a header, a scrolling list and keys split by hairlines
full-height unit with the list cut into a recessed window
content-height unit hanging from the top inline end

variants.reason: A gives a long list the full height to scroll in while title and keys stay put (P6 fixed positions) and keeps the recess for the display (P2); B spends the recess on a list of words, and C changes height with its content and reads as Sheet's twin.

root.why: The drawer is a body of matte plastic with the capped panel radius, inset from the window on all four sides, lit from the top left.

start.why: side start puts the drawer at the inline start, for a screen whose main control sits on the other side, and the slide direction follows it.

inline.why: A drawer shown in place sits in the flow of the page at a fixed place and covers nothing, for previews and docs.

head.why: Title and close key share the top inset line, and a hairline under them sets the header apart from the list that scrolls.

title.why: The title is printed at the emphasis size in the medium weight, so it is the first thing read and it names the drawer.

close.why: A round 44px key at the end of the header closes the drawer by touch, so closing never depends on Escape or the scrim.

content.why: The list takes all the height left between header and keys and scrolls inside itself, so header and keys keep their places.

actions.why: Optional keys sit together at the bottom and inline end under a hairline, where the hand expects the main key.

data-state=open.why: Opening is a state change, so it moves: the body slides in from its edge over motion.release on the decelerating curve while the scrim fades in (D-008).

data-state=closing.why: While it leaves, the drawer slides back out over motion.exit on the accelerating curve and no key or reader reaches it (D-008).

@media prefers-reduced-motion: reduce.why: Under Reduce motion nothing travels; only a fade remains, on motion.hover, which the tokens keep (D-008).

@media forced-colors: active.why: In forced colours the drawer keeps a real border in the text colour and the hairlines use it too, because shadows are dropped.

transform.why: Opening is a state change, so it moves. The only travel is the slide from the drawer's own edge over motion.release in and the shorter motion.exit out (D-008).

opacity.why: The body and the scrim fade with the slide, so both arrive and leave as one change of state, on the same curves (D-008).
